title.suggested: Championship History Recounts Tom Allen's Fights With Mace, McCoole and Goss

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic, on the day of the Corbett-Mitchell fight, ran a history of the championship recounting Tom Allen's loss to Jem Mace at New Orleans, his win over Mike McCoole and his loss to Joe Goss on a foul in 1876.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Thursday Morning, January 25, 1894, page 2. The year of the McCoole fight (1873 in the current summary) is not visible in the clipping.

facts.fact: Jem Mace challenged Allen, who claimed the championship of America, and beat him at New Orleans on May 10 in about 10 rounds lasting 44 minutes, for $5,000
Allen defeated Mike McCoole near St. Louis in seven rounds and again claimed the American championship
Joe Goss challenged Allen and won their fight on September 7, 1876, on a foul, for a purse of $5,000

notes: Right edge cut off: years for the Mace fight and McCoole fight and the round in which Goss won are lost ('Goss won in the ... first round on a foul'). A wider crop from the page image would recover them. Fact dates for Mace fight taken from text ('May 10') plus known 1870 context.
